clue.text: Malign revolutionary supplied with answer by me

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the word after it is read back to front

parts.note: supplied means provided for, fed
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slanders a radical who was helped out with an answer by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malign' looks like an adjective but is a verb here, matching the verb in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them unfairly, the same as damaging their reputation with slander.

clue.text: Hurry with bit of Morse code

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the long signal in Morse, beside the dot

explanation.surface: A telegraph operator rushes to tap out a message.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rushing quickly and the name of the long signal used in telegraph Morse code.

clue.text: Hierarchy secure? Scoff over that

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the second in the column

parts.note: scoff is British slang for food
to secure something is to chain it up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the hierarchy is safe, and mocks the very idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff looks like a verb meaning mock, but as British slang it is a noun meaning grub, placed over CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A food chain is the ranked order of creatures in nature, each eating those beneath it, so it is a pecking order.

clue.text: Time to climb in perfect tower

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: in mint condition means perfect

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An ideal moment to scale a flawless tower.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reversed word reads upwards, so 'climb' fits the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Book, turning brown, about doctor making instrument

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed colour wraps the medical man
turning round sends the colour word back to front

parts.note: sepia is a reddish-brown shade
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A book browns with age while it tells of a medic who takes up an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning brown' reads as a book yellowing with age; turning is the signal acting on the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes are a wind instrument with a bag and drone pipes, strongly associated with Scotland.

clue.text: Bad lot aimed to restrict language soon enough

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the jumble encloses the other word
something bad is spoilt, so the next two words are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder
lingo is an informal word for a language

explanation.surface: A group of rogues tried to clamp down on how people speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad lot' reads as a phrase for rogues, but Bad is the signal and lot is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, at the proper moment, which is another way of saying soon enough.

clue.text: Variable in speech, strangely lacking energy and soul

indicators.note: in places the algebra letter inside the following word
strangely suggests the letters are in an odd order and need rearranging
lacking means going without, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: x and y are the usual algebraic variables
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone talks inconsistently and oddly, without vigour or spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes into SPEECH, one E is removed, and the six letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the Greek-derived word for the human spirit or mind, close in sense to the soul.

clue.text: Son overwhelmed by prize for song

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being swamped and surrounded, so the first letter sits inside the second word

parts.note: the palm is a symbol of victory, a prize
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy wins an award so big it overwhelms him, all for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside PALM: P-S-ALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms in the Bible.

clue.text: Amphibian in cold dish probed by fellow with hesitation

indicators.note: a probe pokes inside, so the dish has the next word pushed into it

parts.note: a salad is a cold dish
a fellow is a man
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A newt turns up in a salad, poked at warily by a nervous diner.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens before the hesitation sound is added on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a lizard-like amphibian with moist skin, related to newts.

clue.text: Villainous organisation of don, cruel in cunning

indicators.note: in places the reordered letters inside the last word

parts.note: sly means cunning

indicators.note: organising things puts them into a new arrangement, so these words are reordered

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A wicked crime syndicate run by a heartless, crafty mafia don.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a mafia boss, but it is just three letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoundrelly is the adjective for behaving like a scoundrel, a rogue, so it means wicked or villainous.

clue.text: Film that's eccentric gives errors, admitting swindle

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so the short word joins the jumbled letters
eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A quirky movie is full of mistakes, including a con.
explanation.walkthrough: DO joins GIVES ERRORS and all thirteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 crime movie about a diamond heist gone wrong.

clue.text: Pointed tool beginning to work, cutting aluminium

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of work

explanation.surface: A sharp implement starts work slicing through metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small spiked hand tool used for punching holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Flower displayed by comrade going around fringes of rally with small song

indicators.note: going around means surrounding the other pieces

parts.note: a chum is a friend or comrade

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its outside edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: outside letters of rally
S is the abbreviation for small
an anthem is a song

explanation.surface: A fellow activist brings flowers to a political rally and leads a short song.
explanation.walkthrough: The friend's word is split in two, wrapping everything else in the middle of the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a showy garden bloom of the daisy family, flowering in autumn.

clue.text: Running van into pipe?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the vehicle sits within the verb

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice, like a bird
a camper is a van fitted out for living in

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how to get a van into a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pipe reads as a tube, but here it is a verb for singing shrilly; the question mark flags the odd senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampering is moving quickly with light steps, like a small animal dashing about.

clue.text: Gossip about fight involving mad character?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the two outer pieces surround the character

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A bit of tittle-tattle about a brawl involving a crazy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About fight' is the pair that does the involving, with the mad character placed between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is a person who talks incessantly, and a gossip is likewise someone who chatters about others.

clue.text: Resort with northern stretch

parts.note: a spa is a resort town with mineral springs
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A northern holiday resort with a long stretch of coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch, the full extent of something from one end to the other.

clue.text: Excessive optimist with a plan only getting confused

indicators.note: confused things are muddled up, so the letters before it are mixed

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An incurable optimist with just a single plan ends up bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollyanna, the heroine of a 1913 novel who always looks on the bright side, became a byword for unreasonable cheerfulness.

clue.text: Hair most important according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: main means most important

explanation.surface: Hair is said to be the most important thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is the long hair on a horse's or lion's neck, and loosely a thick head of human hair.

clue.text: Stewed pear would be yielding a pale colour

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled
yielding means giving up, so one letter is surrendered

parts.note: anagram fodder
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A cooked pear would go soft and turn a washed-out shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the A from PEAR WOULD BE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Powder blue is a soft, light shade of blue, so it is a pale hue.

clue.text: Agree, all awry, to give up good traditional drink

indicators.note: awry means askew, so the letters are knocked out of order
giving something up means losing it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: anagram fodder
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees, though things are going wrong, to give up something good.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from AGREE ALL and rearrange. Real ale is the British term for cask-conditioned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is beer brewed and served in the traditional way, conditioned in the cask, a classic pub drink.

clue.text: Spoil lake, home for fish

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
L is the abbreviation for lake
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Polluting a lake ruins the habitat of the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large ocean game fish with a spear-like upper jaw, prized by sport anglers.

clue.text: Amazing old partner spinning a torrid yarn

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: spinning whirls things round, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A former lover tells a steamy, astonishing tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning a yarn' means telling a story, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary means remarkable, well beyond the usual, which is what amazing describes.

clue.text: Country's leader for now in flowing garment

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the garment

parts.note: the loose robe worn in ancient Rome

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: first letter of now

explanation.surface: A nation's current head appears in a loose robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country's leader' reads as a head of state, but the 's means 'is' and the leader belongs to 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Fixes up bargain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Someone repairs things and gets a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixes up' reads as a phrasal verb, but up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British slang for a bargain, something cheap at the price.

clue.text: Pub sign, one with no odd features

indicators.note: losing the odd features means dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on, keeping the even ones

parts.note: even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A pub sign showing someone with plain, unremarkable features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub sign' looks like one phrase, but Pub alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a public house, a tavern that serves drink and often offers lodging too.

clue.text: General endlessly astute about person beyond control

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: loose means general, not exact, as in a loose translation
canny means shrewd
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A military general, constantly sharp, discusses an unruly subordinate.
explanation.walkthrough: General reads as an army officer, but it is an adjective meaning imprecise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cannon is an unpredictable person who may cause damage, like a gun broken free on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Delight in object reflected in mirror

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the last one

parts.note: a glass is a looking-glass

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in an item seen reflected in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected in mirror' reads as one image; reflected acts on object, and in places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is the state of being happy, joy, which is what delight means as a noun.

clue.text: Update from vicar and a politician

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title
taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: News from the local vicar and an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or give a new look, so it means to modernise or bring up to date.
